speaker: Abelone
dialogue: Thoring runs the inn. Speak to him.

speaker: Acolyte Jenssen
dialogue: Patience. The body needs time to mend.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: I'm going to be a silversmith one day, like my mother and father.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What am I supposed to do? Never leave the house? You want that, Endon?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're closing the stall, and that's final.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: You want to give up now? Out of fear? Is that what we're teaching our daughter?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, why are you and papa fighting?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: We're not fighting, we're just...Why don't I get you something to eat? Mama and papa will talk later.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What should we have tonight?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Something simple, a stew perhaps.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Stew again, papa? I want steak.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Maybe we could spend a litle bit more and buy some meat, Endon.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Maybe. Let me think about it.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, when is Cade coming home?

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: He's off fighting, Adara, with the Stormcloaks. He'll return when the war is over.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Our son joining the Stormcloaks. If this war had never happened, Cade would have joined the Imperial Legion, like grandfather.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, we talked about this... Are you still disappointed in Cade's choice?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: No. I think if I was a young man, I would have done the same.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Can I join the Legion when I grow up?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: If there's still a Legion left, Adara. I'm sure you'd make a great soldier. Just like your brother.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: We sold all those lovely little necklaces you brought me today. Did you make them yourself?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: That's right! Papa helped me with the clasps, but I did all the links on my own.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Adara bends the silver so naturally. Grandmother would have cried if she saw how deft our daughter has become.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Well, I'm proud of both of you. I haven't been so busy since those nobles from Solitude come into the city three years ago.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: I miss those days, before the Forsworn took up arms again, when you could walk the roads in peace.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, dear, please don't.... Save your frustrations for work.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're right, dear. I'm sorry to worry you.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You shouldn't leave Solitude without trying our fish. Best in Skyrim.

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, Jala said you stole an apple from her cart yesterday. Is this true?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Just a little one! I was hungry!

speaker: Greta
dialogue: I'll talk with Jala, dear. I'm sure she'll accept a potato as repayment.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: I suppose. But Svari, we don't steal. We're better than that. Understand?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Eat up, Svari.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: It's all we've got for today. Don't be greedy.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Maybe we'll have better luck tomorrow.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: We'll make it, Greta. We always have so far...

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: If you're looking to purchase goods, I have none to sale. You should head into Riften instead.

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: My darling, you've made me the happiest woman in all Skyrim.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: It brings me joy to hear that, but what possessed you to say that so suddenly?

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: I've already lost a family, and we're about to start a new one. I don't want that to happen again.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: My sweet {{Hide|Leanora|Leonara}}, I will never let anything happen to us. I promise.

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: I'm not so sure the few guards they've assigned to the farm are enough.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: It will have to do. Besides, if it came to blows, I'm sure the {{Hide|Snow-Shod's|Snow-Shods|description=extra apostrophe}} would come out here and assist us.

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: I suppose so. I just fear they won't make it out here in time.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: Just worry about keeping the fields tended and let the Jarl worry about the war.

speaker: Adeber
dialogue: I'm one of the miners. Plenty of ore to dig up around here.

speaker: Orthus Endario
dialogue: Just in time. This is Adelaisa, one of my superiors from the Company.

speaker: Orthus
dialogue: Adelaisa, I'm sorry.

speaker: Adelaisa
dialogue: Sorry isn't good enough, Orthus. There's a lot of gold at stake here, and sniveling isn't going to get it back.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Every now and then someone from the city comes by. Think they aren't used to seeing a Nord working for a Dark Elf.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Make sure the back fence is repaired. I swear I saw some skeevers in nibbling the leaves yesterday.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Oh, no skeevers out here, sir. They can't stand the cold.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe, but the way you burn through all that wood to keep the cabin toasty, they might mistake this place for Elsweyr.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Sorry, sir. These old bones do like a bit of warmth in the evening. There's no need to make fun.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: You just need to remember that there's a war on, and firewood isn't cheap these days.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: I was wondering if you had ordered the shipment of that frostwheat, sir.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Yes, but that fool Endario can't get it in. I'll thrash him when I get back to the city, don't you worry.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: I wasn't wanting to get anyone in trouble, sir. Just wanting to get the new planting started, is all.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Yes, wouldn't want to miss the lush summer we have ahead.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: So, have you ever actually spoken to Captain Lonely-Gale?

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: By the gods, he's just a retired ship's captain.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe to you, but he's just so... his story is...

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: He's just a guard captain. And not a very good one, at that.

speaker: Adonato Leotelli
dialogue: I'm a writer by trade. Not that the people of Skyrim do much reading.

speaker: Adrianne Avenicci
dialogue: I don't claim to be the best blacksmith in Whiterun. Eorlund Gray-Mane's got that honor. The man's steel is legendary. All I ask is a fair chance.

speaker: Adrianne
dialogue: I just can't fill an order that size on my own. Why don't you swallow that stubborn pride of yours and ask Eorlund Gray-Mane for help?

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Ha! I'd sooner bend my knee to Ulfric Stormcloak. Besides, Gray-Mane would never make steel for the Legion.

speaker: Adrianne
dialogue: Have it your way. I'll take the job, but don't expect a miracle.

speaker: Aduri Sarethi
dialogue: This place is boring. Nothing but the same thing every day.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Aduri, how come the fields haven't been tilled like I asked?

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Because it's boring. The fields are going to do fine... you don't have to dote over them so much.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Boring? That food is paying for everything. If we lose even a single crop, we could starve or be forced to beg. I won't have it!

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: All right, I understand. I'll do it tomorrow, okay? Just get off my back.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Have you decided if I can head up to Solitude yet? I hear it's the best place to meet someone who may be willing to teach me to paint.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: I'm sorry, Aduri, not this year. Perhaps next year after the harvest, I don't know. There's so much to do.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: It's not going to be next year, nor the year after that! You just care about this farm more than you care about me!

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Painting won't put food on the table, but our crops will. Be patient Aduri... it will happen someday, I promise.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Where did all these pretty red plants come from?

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Remember Uncle Sinderion? These are the plants he was searching for... the Crimson Nirnroot.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: They're beautiful. I can see why he wanted to find them.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: One day, these beautiful plants will make us famous and we can finally move off of this farm... thanks to Sinderion.

speaker: Aela the Huntress
dialogue: Something has shifted in the moons, brother.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I told you, this is the whelp that Vilkas mentioned.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Ah, yes. I heard you gave him quite a thrashing.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Don't let Vilkas catch you saying that.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Did you call me?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Of course we did, icebrain. Show this newblood where the rest of the whelps sleep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: New blood? Oh, hello. I'm Farkas. Come, follow me.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: Who will start?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'll do it. Before the ancient flame... We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: At this loss... We weep.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: For the fallen... We shout.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: And for ourselves... We take our leave.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: His spirit is departed. Members of the Circle, let us withdraw to the Underforge, to grieve our last together.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: The old man had one wish before he died. And he didn't get it. It's as simple as that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Being moon-born is not so much of a curse as you might think, Vilkas.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: That's fine for you. But he wanted to be clean. He wanted to meet Ysgramor and know the glories of Sovngarde. But all that was taken from him.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And you avenged him.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Kodlak did not care for vengeance.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: No, Farkas, he didn't. And that's not what this is about. We should be honoring Kodlak, no matter our own thoughts on the blood.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You're right. It's what he wanted, and he deserved to have it.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Kodlak used to speak of a way to cleanse his soul, even in death. You know the legends of the Tomb of Ysgramor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: There the souls of Harbingers will heed the call of northern steel. We can't even enter the tomb without Wuuthrad, and it's in pieces, like it has been for a thousand years.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: And dragons were just stories. And the elves once ruled Skyrim. Just because something is, doesn't mean it must be. The blade is a weapon. A tool. Tools are meant to be broken. And repaired.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Is that? Did you repair the blade?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You wanted to see me?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I worry that you've been spending too many nights out.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Where I go is my business. If you have a concern about my honor, bring it before the Circle.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: You forget yourself, young one.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to snap. Just... these hunters. We're all on edge.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: That's why it's best to not mistake foolhardiness for bravery.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: How goes the hunt?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Skjor's heard rumors of a bear the size of a mammoth in Hammerfell. We're going to seek it out.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: What glorious prey. Come back alive, and with stories to tell!

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: All these younglings scampering around.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Worried one of them is going to take your place?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Some of them might try. But that's not what I'm worried about.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: What then?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: That they might get themselves killed.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: By you?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: They should be so lucky.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Are you prepared for tonight's hunt?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I've been thinking we need to be more... discreet.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: There's nothing wrong with what we're doing.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You know the old man doesn't like it. Let's just not be too obvious.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I've heard some rumors... about you and Skjor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And if you want to keep having ears, you'll pretend you didn't.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Is it not allowed?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: It's not exactly forbidden, but even so... it's not true. So that's that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: How do you manage to hold your ground like that?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: You have to remember, it's not about strength. It's about leverage.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: But strength doesn't hurt.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Well, no. I'm just saying there's more to defense than muscle.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I've never seen Mjoll this upset about anything. The city really gets to her.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I had another run-in with the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: Be careful, Mjoll. The Thieves Guild has Maven Black-Briar at her back. One snap of her fingers, and you could end up in Riften Jail... or worse.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: They represent the reason I'm here. I can't just ignore them, Aerin.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I know. I just don't want you to leave; you're the only good thing that's happened to this city in a long time.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: Well, you were right. These so called 'Gutter Saints' live in the sewers beneath.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I suspected as much. The real question now is do we do something about it ourselves or do we speak to the Jarl?

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I say we go down there and clear the place out, just like old times.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: No, my friend. That would be reckless. We have to help, but help in a way that doesn't directly place anyone in harm's way. For now, give this 'Ratway' a wide berth.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Sometimes I'm not certain that the people of Riften want to be helped.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I think some of them do, Lady Mjoll. They're just too frightened to step up and do something about it like you are.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, you never cease to amaze me. You always see the good in everything.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: It's only because I've had an excellent teacher.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: You've been in Riften for quite some time now, Lady Mjoll. I fear that you soon may leave us.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Riften has problems of its own. Now is not the time for exploration and discovery.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I'm relieved to hear you say that. If you were to leave, I'd miss you terribly.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, I owe you my life. It would take a threat to all of Skyrim for me to depart.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, have you seen my ring? The one with the inscription?

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: No, I haven't. Don't tell me you've lost it.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I hope not. That ring is irreplaceable.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I'll look around the house and if I find it, I'll bring it to you right away.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Peryite, heed our call and deem us worthy. Our leader, Orchendor, has led us here, and for that we are thankful. He has shown us that our suffering is not a punishment, but a blessing.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, a blessing. For many months we have sought your guidance, yet we have heard nothing from you. If we do not please you, give us a sign so we may understand why.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Yes, a sign. We are lost without your guidance. On the ninth of Rain's Hand, our prayers went unanswered, yet here we stand unfaltering in our belief that you will soon show yourself to us.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, show yourself to us. Until that day, we will continue to devote our lives to you and suffer for you.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Yes, suffer for you.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: I'm sorry to wake you, my brother, but I have a request from Orchendor.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, what is it?

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: He requests more barrels of ichor to be delivered to the Arcanex tonight.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: This is the reason you wake me? I already have Orchendor's request taken care of.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: I'm sorry, my brother.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Now, leave me to my sleep. My strength and patience are waning.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Yes, my brother. Forgive me. May the blessing of Peryite be with you.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, yes. As with you. Now, off with you.

speaker: Afflicted Refugee
dialogue: Are you finished ogling the grotesque? I suppose I should be grateful you didn't simply attack me.
